goal: Send one Discord DM for a failed Twitch chat bot token and a recovery DM when token health returns.
acceptance: Persist only health timestamps and short failure codes, never token material
Validate the current token hourly and retain the existing refresh cadence
Health write failures do not disable chat
Read producer-owned outage episodes only while the bot service runs and monitoring is enabled
Reuse incident delay of 90 seconds and idempotent broker delivery
Persist recovery delivery and retry state
Pass affected package build, formatting, linting, token tests and isolated PostgreSQL watchdog tests
Receive review gate ALLOW, commit and push; no main merge or deployment
integration: Apply the new migration before restarting tb-bot and the watchdog. Integrator owns deployment and live DM verification.
transition_rules: Intentional native-chat disablement pauses token monitoring and supersedes pending alerts without sending recovery.
Outage delivery is a stable historical event; recovery uses a distinct durable idempotency key and retry state.
Credential state and success or failure health publication share the same critical section.
Boot success is published only after the persisted bot identity has been bound.
Both token notification phases describe historical validation observations, never present chat availability; HTTP errors can leave a usable cached token.
Retries persist observation time, not retry time; transactional statement timeouts prevent timed-out writes from overtaking newer observations.
Outage and recovery delivery failures have independent durable first-error markers.
Bot-token incident boundaries use failure and successful validation event timestamps, not watchdog polling time; notification eligibility uses the actual recovered outage duration.
An intervening success closes an open token incident even if a newer failure already exists; that newer failure opens a separate incident.
Every boot and runtime transition is queued and retried in order without merging, including after publisher handles are dropped.
The first failure opens an episode; repeated failures preserve its start; the first subsequent success closes it and later successes preserve its end.
Watchdog observations use durable episode ids and original boundaries, including fully recovered episodes first seen after 90 seconds.
Disabling monitoring suppresses prior episodes and closes any open episode without recovery notification.
